case.source_text:
Synthetic nurse note for software testing. No real patient data.

The driver reports that vehicles approaching from the left sometimes appear suddenly, although he can read the central letters on a chart and denies constant double vision; he also describes occasional overlapping headlights after long night shifts, which were absent during the consultation. A field printout shows a binocular horizontal extent of 135 degrees, but carries a poor-fixation warning and does not clearly document the vertical test extent, central defects or whether the result is stable over time.

He recalls being told that an old injury left one eye less useful, while an earlier letter records vision in both eyes and no current specialist opinion confirms monocularity. A handwritten acuity entry of 6/9 is not assigned to an eye or labelled as corrected, and the driver alternates between an older pair of glasses and a recently purchased pair during work.

Blood-pressure treatment was increased two weeks earlier after several elevated home readings, and he reports brief light-headedness when standing without a definite blackout. Today's BP 162/96 mmHg is a single seated observation; the nurse has not attributed the visual complaints to blood pressure, established persistent hypertension from the available entries or treated the unreliable field result as a confirmed measurement.
